parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: An initially uncharged capacitor X, of capacitance *C*, is gradually charged so that the final potential difference (p.d.) between its plates is *V* and the final charge is *Q*.
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.1, sketch the variation of charge with p.d. for capacitor X as the p.d. increases from 0 to *V*.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of *Q* and *V*, for the work *W* done on capacitor X during the charging process. Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
Another capacitor Y is initially uncharged. The fully charged capacitor X in (b) is now connected to capacitor Y, as shown in Fig. 7.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The capacitance of capacitor Y is 3*C*.
parts.text:
Complete Table 7.1 to show expressions, in terms of *Q* and *V*, for the final p.d.s across, and the final charges on, the two capacitors. Use the space below for any working that you need.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State whether the total energy stored in the two capacitors is less than, the same as, or greater than the energy initially stored in capacitor X.
